slides.description: Full-bleed illustrated top-down city map at dusk, framed like an open-world game. A central player avatar stands between labeled landmarks including the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Neon Dragon Casino, Bank & Realty Office, The Underworld, and Whispering Temple Chapel. Across the top, a bold title reads “CAPITAL SYNDICATE” with the subtitle “Financial Reality Engine.” A large objective badge says “Build your way to $10M,” surrounded by route icons: briefcase/day job, stock chart, crypto coin, casino chips, house, fishing rod, and a warning icon for scams and black-market deals. Small callouts on buildings say “Every stop is playable” and “Minigames, not menus.”
slides.narration: Imagine GTA-style open-world freedom, but the currency is financial power. In Capital Syndicate, you live in the city and build toward ten million through jobs, markets, casinos, real estate, fishing—or the criminal underworld, with every building hiding a playable puzzle.

slides.description: Dynamic three-panel action composition. Left: the player drives a bright sports car through city streets with a drifting motion trail. Center: colorful casino tables show Blackjack cards, spinning Slots, Poker chips, and a roulette-style risk meter. Right: a red-alert police chase leads to a jail screen with three large choices: “Bribe,” “Talk Your Way Out,” and “Escape.” A progression arrow connects “Crime” to “Police Chase” to “Jail” to “Freedom,” emphasizing consequences rather than a game-over screen.
slides.narration: The most visual routes are pure arcade energy: drive across the city, hit the casino, and watch luck reshape your bankroll. Go criminal, and the game fires back with police chases, jail, and risky choices to bribe, negotiate, or escape.

slides.description: A large smartphone UI dominates the slide. The Social/X feed shows AI-generated posts from named historical-persona NPCs, with sentiment arrows pushing a stock chart sharply upward and downward. Beside it, an NPC conversation window displays free-text chat and a heart/date icon, labeled “Live AI conversation—not scripted dialogue.” A third phone panel shows the AI Assistant answering: “How do I hedge this position?” Caption at bottom: “AI content → social sentiment → market movement.”
slides.narration: AI is part of the game’s bloodstream, not decoration. A generated social feed changes sentiment and stock prices, historical figures can be chatted with—or dated—through live conversations, and your phone assistant can answer any question in the world.

slides.description: A clean milestone ladder runs horizontally across the center: “$50K → $250K → $1M → $5M → $10M,” with each rung growing larger and brighter toward a gold “REAL WIN” finish line. Under the ladder, route cards show day job, trading, casino, property, and crime as different ways to advance. In the lower-right corner, a smaller faded badge reads “$1B FLEX GOAL — optional bragging rights,” explicitly separated from the gold finish line by a dashed line and the label “past the real win.”
slides.narration: The real win condition is a tiered climb: fifty thousand, two-fifty, one million, five million, and finally ten million dollars. A billion is only an optional flex goal for players who want to keep playing—it is not the target.

slides.description: A stylized command-center diagram shows ten connected specialist agent cards orbiting a central game build. The cards are labeled: Producer, Game Designer, World Builder, Gameplay Engineer, Art Director, Visual Polish, Technical Artist, Audio Director, Writer, and QA Tester. Each card has a tiny icon matching its role, while the center reads “One coordinated AI fleet,” with a footer: “Narrow jobs • shared production flow • human product owner.” A small contrast callout says “Not one generalist assistant.”
slides.narration: The game is also a lesson in agentic systems. Ten specialized AI subagents divide the work—from producer and world-builder to gameplay, art, audio, writing, and live-browser QA—instead of asking one generalist assistant to do everything.

slides.description: A production roadmap slide with a large “~6 DAYS LEFT” header and a countdown panel reading “Day Left: 30.” On the left, a red crossed-out card says “No new prison prologue world”; beside it, a gold card says “New capstone: $10M win cutscene.” On the right, a six-item punch list appears with checkboxes: “Tighten storyline,” “Audit stock exchange,” “Add casino/arcade minigames,” “Straighten car-theft → police → jail → bribe flow,” “Confirm church hub is done,” and “Verify Lisa romance path.” A footer warning reads “Phone check costs 1 day • Day 0 = game over.”
slides.narration: With about six days left, the scope gets sharper: no brand-new prison world, but a focused win cutscene when the player crosses ten million. The finish line is a six-item punch list, plus a thirty-day clock where checking your phone costs a day—and reaching zero ends the run.
